Proposed dissertation direction

Environmental Stress Histories and Benthic Habitat Composition of Indonesian Coral Reefs

1. Background

  • Indonesia contains approximately 40,209 km² of coral reefs distributed across more than 17,000 islands.[1]
  • Environmental pressure varies among regions and through time, while reef composition varies within and among reef areas.[3]
  • Field surveys provide essential local detail, while satellite observations extend coverage across larger and more frequently observed areas.[2]

2. Current remote-sensing information

CRESIRegional and repeated environmental-stress information, but no detailed benthic composition.[3]
+
Benthic mappingDetailed habitat classes; mapping consistency and local evaluation affect reliability.[4] The evaluation site is Tidung.
→
Missing connectionNo comparable benthic information for reef areas representing different CRESI histories.

3. Research gap

CRESI shows differences in environmental-stress history among Indonesian reefs, but comparable benthic maps are not yet available to examine whether their present habitat composition also differs.

4. Research importance

Wider reef coverageCRESI identifies contrasting reef areas beyond one local site.
Consistent comparisonOne workflow produces the same benthic classes across selected reefs.
Monitoring valueThe results can guide reef selection for field surveys and continued monitoring.

5. Research aim

To compare benthic habitat composition among selected Indonesian reefs with different CRESI environmental-stress histories.

6. Main research question

Do Indonesian reefs with different environmental-stress histories also show differences in satellite-mapped benthic composition?

Connection between the studies

  • CRESI defines the environmental histories and guides reef selection.
  • Tidung provides the reference information needed to evaluate the benthic-mapping workflow.
  • The evaluated workflow provides comparable benthic information for the selected reefs.
  • The final analysis compares benthic composition among the CRESI environmental histories.
Interpretation: the comparison tests association. It does not claim that environmental stress caused the observed benthic composition.

Research components

Three Studies in One Research Sequence

STUDY 1

Environmental-stress histories across Indonesia

How do environmental-stress histories differ among Indonesian reef areas?

InputsSST · DHW · PAR · water clarity · chlorophyll · bleaching observations
AnalysisCRESI-Mamba · pathway contributions · frequency and duration
ResultEnvironmental history for each reef
Used nextSelection of contrasting reef areas
STUDY 2

Benthic-mapping evaluation at Tidung

How reliably can Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope map benthic habitat at Tidung?

InputsSentinel-2 · PlanetScope · UAV reference map · underwater observations
AnalysisImage correction · depth and benthic processing · accuracy evaluation
ResultClass accuracy · sensor and depth effects · uncertainty
Used nextOne evaluated Sentinel-2 workflow
STUDY 3

Benthic composition across selected Indonesian reefs

Do reefs with different environmental-stress histories show differences in satellite-mapped benthic composition?

InputsSelected CRESI reef groups · comparable Sentinel-2 imagery
AnalysisCommon mapping workflow · confidence checks · composition comparison
ResultCoral, seaweed, seagrass, sand, and other percentages
Final testAssociation with environmental history
Supporting method: the semi-analytical algorithm is applied in Study 2 and Study 3. The PhD work evaluates and applies the workflow and examines its uncertainty.

Expected contribution

Dissertation Outputs

Scientific outputs

  • Environmental-stress histories for Indonesian reef areas.
  • A locally evaluated Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope benthic-mapping workflow.
  • Comparable Sentinel-2 benthic maps for selected reef areas.
  • Benthic-composition comparison among contrasting environmental histories.
  • Uncertainty and conditions for transferring the workflow beyond Tidung.

What the dissertation tests

Whether reefs with different environmental-stress histories also show differences in satellite-mapped benthic composition.

Main contribution

An approach for comparing benthic habitat composition among Indonesian reefs with different environmental-stress histories.
